# **Background**

The CPQ Managed Package had a feature where for End of Sale products, a pricing admin could define a replacement product, so that when someone goes to renew the end of sale product, it’s automatically substituted for the replacement product.

This partner has raised it as a a CPQ Parity issue:  
[https://salesforce-external.slack.com/archives/C06UK3M3PE2/p1759178272717649](https://salesforce-external.slack.com/archives/C06UK3M3PE2/p1759178272717649)  
"does anyone know of functionality in Rev Cloud that is similar to the Salesforce CPQ "SBQQ\_\_RenewalProduct\_\_c" functionality? For example, my asset for Product 1 is coming up for renewal. Product 1 needs to be replaced with Product 2 on renewal quotes since Product 1 is end of life."

To prove that this feature existed in the CPQ package, here’s a link to help documentation about the CPQ field  "SBQQ\_\_RenewalProduct\_\_c": [https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.cpq\_product\_fields.htm\&type=5](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.cpq_product_fields.htm&type=5)  
“Product that replaces this product on renewal. Use it to quote a different SKU when renewing.  
The Renewal Product field can't target a product with a consumption schedule.

You can’t replace a renewable subscription product with a one-time product.”

Here’s where that help topic showed up in the help documentation, showing that folks think of the product modeling side of this requirement as a PCM issue:  
**![][image1]**

# **Idea Part 1: PCM**

Desired Business Outcome: A product/pricing admin wants to end of sale or end of life a product.  They want to specify a replacement product, so that when a renewal gets generated with this product, it’s automatically substituted with the replacement product.

System/User Flow

1. For a Product2 record, admin specifies a Renewal Product

Notes:

* TODO: Check in with Saras on what PCM did for EOL/EOS already.  Product2 has an EOL Date field, but how does one denote Product Status?  Is it just by unchecking the Active flag?  
* Just do exactly what the CPQ package did.  It worked and customers like it.  There’s no need to over design or over complicate this.  Customers like it so much that we have a VOC where customers are asking us to just implement it like the CPQ package  
* No need to validate if they’re in the same price book or anything.  We’ll handle a bunch of things downstream when generating the renewal.  Keep it simple.

# **Idea Part 2: Renewal**

Desired Business Outcome: As a sales rep, I create a renewal containing a product that’s been end of lifed or end of saled.  When the renewal is generated, automatically substitute the product with a replacement product (if one has been specified).  Set the price to list price, regardless of the original asset’s pricing source.  Set the qty to the original asset’s qty and set the term count to the original asset’s renewal term

Example:

* ‘Sales Cloud Performance Edition’ is a Product2 record that a pricing / product admin has deemed end of life  
  * In the ‘Sales Cloud Performance Edition’ Product2 record, the Renewal Product is ‘Agentforce Sales Unlimited Edition’  
    * Where List Price for ‘Agentforce Sales Unlimited Edition’ is $300/user/month  
* Crowdstrike owns 1,000 licenses of Sales Cloud Performance Edition termed 1/1/2025-12/31/2026  
  * Renewal Term: 2 years  
  * Last Transaction Price \= $200/user/month  
  * Asset Pricing Source \= Last Transaction Price (LTP)

System/User Flow:

1. User starts a renewal for ‘Sales Cloud Performance Edition’, with a start date of 1/1/2027 (aka on-time renewal) on 12/15/2026  
2. System automatically detects that ‘Sales Cloud Performance Edition’ is end of lifed, and that the replacement product is ‘Agentforce Sales Unlimited Edition’  
3. Renewal Quote then has this QLI:  
   1. Product: ‘Agentforce Sales Unlimited Edition’  
   2. Qty: 1,000  
   3. List Price: $300/user/month  
   4. Discount %: 0  
   5. Net Unit Price: $300/user/month  
   6. Start-End Date: 1/1/2027-12/31/2028 (because original asset renewal term was 2 years)  
   7. Total Price: $300/user/month x 1,000 users x 24 months \= $7.2mm  
4. Quote to Order is executed  
5. Order is assetized  
6. New Asset is generated:  
   1. Name:  ‘Agentforce Sales Unlimited Edition’  
   2. Qty: 1,000  
   3. ASP  
      1. 1/1/2027 \- 12/31/2028, Qty= 1,000  
   4. Asset Action  
      1. Action=Initial Sale, Qty=1000, NUP \= $300, Total Price \= $7.2mm  
      2. Action Date: 12/15/2026  
7. (NEW & IMPORTANT) Create a linkage between the old asset and the replacement asset so that reports can be generated that answer these questions:  
   1. For customers that owned the old asset, how many of them renewed to the replacement product?  
   2. Since we’re creating a proper linkage, go back and apply this to swaps too so that folks can answer the question ‘for people that owned Product A, how many of them swapped to a different product, and what product did they swap to?’  
      1. Currently answering this question requires a complicated multi-join query

# **Additional requirements across the other ARC features**

* Contract Pricing  
  * If ‘Sales Cloud Performance Edition’ had a contract price, ignore the contract price.  The contract price was for the old product.  All bets are off with the new replacement product.  
* Flavors of renewals that need to be supported for this:  
  * Early Renewal  
  * Renew expired asset / late renewal  
  * As-is Renewal  
    * If the original asset had lots, collapse the lots and reprice the total qty at list price for the replacement product  
  * Co-term  
    * If there’s a contract specified in the renewal order, co-term to the end of the contract and ignore the asset pricing term (TODO: Ask an engineer to check if this is current behavior)  
  * Ramped Assets  
    * For a ramped asset, when you’re in the last segment, it’s generally treated like any other asset.  Do the same for this feature  
  * Auto Renewal:  
    * Auto Renewal automatically substitutes the replacement product, if applicable  
  * Swaps/Upgrades/Downgrades  
    * A replacement product asset can be the source for a swap, upgrade, or downgraded  
  * FDO  
    * A replacement product asset can be the source for a swap, upgrade, or downgraded  
  * Backdated Renewal  
    * Replacement product logic can be applied to a backdated renewal  
* Out of Scope:  
  * Rollback: In general, we don’t support rolling back a renewal  
  * Renewal Uplift & CPI Uplift: If a previous CPI uplift or renewal uplift has been negotiated, that is ignored  
* Reference to [Asset Lifecycle Features](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1nydjkLzdI_PzysqW_yOkX7GeYFmEFk_Bzv9wiAHorb4/edit?gid=1638583986#gid=1638583986) to cross check that we’ve thought about all the other ARC features
